Breastfeeding Tip of the Week

Watch your baby, not the clock.

Many parents worry about how long a feed should last. The truth is that every baby is different. Some babies feed efficiently in 10–15 minutes, while others may take longer.

✅ Signs your baby is feeding well:
• At least 6 wet diapers per day after the first week
• Steady weight gain
• Appears satisfied after most feeds

💡 Breastfeeding is not only nutrition—it's also comfort, bonding, and emotional security for your baby.

If you're experiencing pain, difficulty latching, concerns about milk supply, or worries about your baby's weight gain, early support can make a big difference.

👩‍⚕️ Dr. Soumya Renji
Pediatrician & Lactation Support
Helping families build a confident breastfeeding journey.

Protect Your Child from Influenza This Season

Influenza (flu) is more than just a common cold. It can cause high fever, severe cough, breathing difficulties, ear infections, pneumonia, and may lead to hospitalization, especially in young children.

✅ The best protection against influenza is annual vaccination.

Why vaccinate?
• Reduces the risk of severe illness and hospitalization
• Helps protect infants, grandparents, and other vulnerable family members
• Reduces missed school days and parental work absences
• Recommended every year, as flu viruses change over time

👶 Influenza vaccination is recommended for all children aged 6 months and older, unless advised otherwise by your doctor.

A healthy child can still get severe flu. Prevention is always better than treatment.

Talk to your pediatrician about whether your child is due for the influenza vaccine this season.

👩‍⚕️ Dr. Soumya Renji
Pediatrician | Vaccination | Newborn Care | Child Development | Breastfeeding Support

Fever Myths Every Parent Should Know

Fever is one of the most common reasons parents worry, but many myths about fever can cause unnecessary anxiety.

❌ Myth 1: Every fever needs antibiotics
✅ Most fevers in children are caused by viral infections, which do not improve with antibiotics.

❌ Myth 2: Higher fever means a more serious illness
✅ The child's overall condition, activity level, hydration, and breathing are often more important than the temperature itself.

❌ Myth 3: Fever will cause brain damage
✅ Fever due to common infections does not cause brain damage. Brain injury occurs only at extremely high body temperatures, which are usually not caused by routine infections.

❌ Myth 4: Fever must be completely normal before the next medicine dose
✅ Fever medicines help your child feel comfortable. It's okay if the temperature doesn't become completely normal.



💡 Remember: Treat the child, not just the number on the thermometer.

Seek medical attention if your child has difficulty breathing, persistent vomiting, dehydration, unusual drowsiness, seizures, or if you have concerns about their condition.

Pediatrician | Newborn Care | Vaccination | Child Development | Breastfeeding Support

✔ Reduced Depth Perception
